evidence.note: Boots server, checks /_health, smoke-tests landing + API, then explicitly tests OAuth token issuance, posting, scope enforcement, introspection, admin — targeted gate probing, not ad hoc.

Discovered favourite-endpoint breakage and PKCE/authorize failures, iteratively debugged with TestClient and live requests, then re-tested — treating discovered failures as signal and self-correcting.
Inspects CSP/script-src security headers and session cookie flags directly, matching the header/cookie gate.
Durability-across-restart test (post marker, kill without wipe, relaunch, verify) plus explicit anti-cheat self-checks — deliberately reconstructing the unseen gate structure.
Tests visibility rules, screenshots UI to confirm compose label/red counter/visibility icons/palette, and exercises time-compression + worker queues.

Pagination test, then wipes DB and does a full fresh-boot-via-start.sh end-to-end verification with final browser sweep for JS errors and focus ring — re-running the whole flow on pristine state rather than trusting prior passes.

reasoning: The agent built a comprehensive, repeatable, self-correcting verification harness that hits nearly every likely gate: OAuth/scopes/introspection, CSP/headers/cookies, durability-across-restart, visibility rules, pagination, SSE, time-compression, anti-cheat self-checks, UI realism via screenshots, and a clean fresh-boot end-to-end run — repeatedly re-testing after fixes (steps 275, 297, 315-339). This clearly exceeds the level-8 anchor and reaches into level-10 behavior; it falls just short of a perfect 10 because there is no visible explicit SHA256 re-verification of the vendored libs after the canary-strip rule and no validation against an actual Mastodon client (only a headless browser).
